Jordan (ACME): Hi team — evaluating Redwood BYO-HSM for an upcoming POC. Primary asks from compliance: 1) rotation without downtime, 2) audit artifacts for rotation, 3) emergency compromise workflow. Who can confirm?
Aisha (Sales): Hi Jordan — we can support that. Standard BYO-HSM POC covers integration + audit support. For emergency/compromise we have a documented runbook but will need to capture any custom custodian rules in the SOW.
Jordan (ACME): Great. Can you sketch the standard rotation sequence we can share with Infosec? They need explicit steps and a time estimate.
Tom (Solutions Eng): Standard flow we run: 
1) Provision new KEK (customer HSM or supported cloud HSM)
2) Start background rewrap job for DEKs (data encryption keys) with streaming checkpoints
3) Flip envelope key pointer atomically at config layer
4) Monitor rewrap progress; keep old KEK valid for read until rewrap finishes
Estimated duration: automated ~30-90 minutes for typical dataset sizes; manual ceremony can be hours depending on custodians.
Riya (Security): Important to note: if the HSM is air-gapped and requires physical key ceremony, the rotation window depends on custodian availability. Also we provide signed manifests and HSM provenance logs as proof.
Jordan (ACME): For audit artifacts, can you provide sample outputs? JSON logs, signed manifests, maybe a small example of the rewrap job metrics.
Tom (Solutions Eng): Yes — we provide: 
- rotation-manifest.json (signed by Redwood and optionally by your custodian)
- rewrap_job_metrics.csv (counts, start/end, failures)
- sample HSM-provenance.log (sequence of wrap/unwrap ops)
I'll attach a trimmed JSON example in the SOW appendix.
Maya (ACME-InfoSec): Does Redwood's platform ever hold plaintext keys during rotation? We need an explicit statement for legal.
Riya (Security): Short answer: No. The platform never writes plaintext DEKs to persistent Redwood storage. Rewrap is performed using wrapped keys and HSM unwrap/rewrap operations. We can add a security note to the SOW: 'No plaintext DEKs are persisted outside customer HSM boundary.'
Jordan (ACME): Billing question: who pays for the compute involved in rewrap heavy jobs? Also any network egress costs?
Liam (Finance Ops): Rewrap compute is billed as part of platform usage (normal API/compute charges); if you want Redwood to run it during the POC we include an allowance (e.g., up to 40h). Cross-region egress remains customer's cloud egress. If you want a dedicated engineering block in SOW (fixed price) we can include that separately.
Jordan (ACME): Our custodian policy requires 2-of-3 quorum for any key ceremony. Any compatibility issues?
Tom (Solutions Eng): We're compatible. If your ceremony requires multiple human approvals, we integrate via your remote-signing workflow. If physical presence is required, travel/time will be outlined in the SOW. For remote quorum we can wire up an HSM workflow or a signing proxy.
Jordan (ACME): Emergency key rotation — if we suspect compromise, we need a fast path that doesn't wait for a full ceremony. What do you offer?
Tom (Solutions Eng): Emergency path (high-level):
- Freeze writes (optional depending on tolerance)
- Spin up emergency KEK in pre-approved HSM (requires at least one custodian auth)
- Prioritize rewrap of highest-sensitivity DEKs first
- Complete bulk rewrap using accelerated job runner
- Post-action: full ceremony to replace emergency KEK with quorum-approved KEK and rotate again if needed
We provide a pre-approved emergency approver list in SOW so approvals are quick.
Riya (Security): We'll flag emergency actions in audit logs and mark them for retained forensic review. Recommend defining 'emergency' in SOW to avoid accidental misuse.
Jordan (ACME): Good. Can we get a sample SOW clause for rotation SLAs and emergency approval matrix?
Aisha (Sales): Yes — we'll draft two SOW options: (A) Basic POC (includes integration, 40h support, audit artifacts) (B) POC + ceremony automation + emergency workflow + dedicated eng hours. We'll also include sample SLO language for rotation: target automated rotation complete within 2 hours 95% p90 during normal ops, emergency path within 4 hours from approval.
Maya (ACME-InfoSec): We need sample audit JSON to verify parsers. Can you include a 10-line JSON example of a rotation-manifest and a tiny HSM operation log?
Tom (Solutions Eng): Will include. Example will show timestamped wrap/unwrap entries, operator IDs, and signed digest.
Jordan (ACME): One more: key retirement policy. After rotation, how long is the old KEK kept? Our policy is 90 days hold for recovery. Is that supported?
Riya (Security): We support configurable retention. Default is retain old KEK wrapped metadata until rewrap completes + 30 days. For 90-day hold we can include that as an SOW option; note it increases storage and audit retention costs.
Liam (Finance Ops): If you want 90-day retention, we'll specify retention tier and costs in the SOW appendix. Typically it's a small monthly fee per key archived plus log-retention charges.
Jordan (ACME): Perfect. Please upload the SOW snippet, runbook, small sample logs, and a cost appendix. We'll circulate internally.
Aisha (Sales): On it — Tom will upload by EOD. Also setting up a follow-up call to review SOW choices next Wed.
OpsBot: SOW upload link generated: https://redwood.example/sow/1719609876-poc-rotation-playbook (access: redwood-sales + ACME read).
Tom (Solutions Eng): Uploaded: SOW appendix + 3-page rotation runbook + sample logs. Link above.
Maya (ACME-InfoSec): Downloaded and starting review. Thanks everyone.
Jordan (ACME): Thanks all, this helps. We'll revert with any redline.
